structured_output.world_model:
Only one measurement exists: E000, the template demo (3 SGD steps on 64 images). It gave accuracy 0.0122 (about chance, 1%) and time 0.14 s. That tells me three things. First, the harness works and the fixed overhead of prepare+train with a tiny model is small, well under 1 s. This is the only measured evidence on H3, and it only bounds the non-compute fixed costs. Second, the time cost of an airbench-style run will be dominated by compute and by first-use costs (cuDNN autotune, lazy kernel init, compile). Neither was measured here. Third, I have no measured noise for accuracy or time.

Everything else is an extrapolation from priors, not from this table. In particular, I have not measured that the airbench96 port reaches 75% at 9 epochs. CIFAR-100 at 75% in about 9 epochs is aggressive. The reference airbench96 recipe is for CIFAR-10 at 96%, and the CIFAR-100 transfer is untested here. My prior is that the first port lands around 0.70-0.76. Time for 9 epochs of a 128/384/576-wide net on an A100 is probably 8-15 s eager, so the 9.5 s target in H1.1.1 is likely missed in eager mode.

Mechanisms I believe, in order of confidence:
1. Epochs times cost per epoch sets the time. Accuracy is a smooth function of epochs, so epoch count is the main dial.
2. Putting data on the GPU gives a big win over the template pipeline. The template already did this for 64 images, so this is unmeasured.
3. Compile and fp16 channels_last help by 10-30%, but compile in build is risky: recompiles in timed code, and eval shapes.
4. Muon, EMA and progressive resizing are uncertain, with small effects of a few percent either way, and are likely within noise at 3 seeds.

Noise: unknown. I assume per-seed accuracy std is 0.2-0.4 pp, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15-0.25 pp. I assume time noise is 1-3%.

Unsure about: whether the first port clears 0.753, how much the whitening and Dirac init matter, and how expensive the fixed costs are in a real run.

forecasts.reason: The 9-epoch CIFAR-100 port likely lands near the 0.753 bar, and eager time is probably above 9.5 s.
Going to 10 epochs is likely, since the port probably misses the bar. Accuracy should rise about 0.3-0.8 pp and time about 10%.
Compile, channels_last and a fused optimizer likely cut compute by 10-25%, but there is some risk of fixed-cost leakage.
The EMA gain is probably about 0.1-0.4 pp, close to the noise.
Identical reruns should give times within about 2% and per-seed std of about 0.2-0.4 pp.
Dropping the ragged batch saves a small amount, and the 0.3 s threshold is borderline. Accuracy is unchanged within noise.
Muon is untuned on this backbone and the first attempt is unlikely to beat tuned SGD by 10% in epochs.
Time saving is probably 10-20%, but the accuracy loss may exceed 0.2 pp, so the combined claim is uncertain.

cruxes: What 3-seed accuracy does the plain 9-epoch airbench port reach on CIFAR-100? If it is at or above 0.753, I001 is already feasible. If it is below about 0.74, we need 11 or more epochs.
What is the eager time per epoch on the A100 under the 4-CPU pin, and how large are the fixed first-use costs (cuDNN autotune, lazy init) in the timed region?
What are the per-seed accuracy std and time noise? These set how much margin above 0.753 is needed.
